risk: Reconciliations are prepared as a formality, so differences accumulate in accounts nobody scrutinises and errors or misappropriation persist for years.
audit_objective: Assess whether reconciliations are complete, timely and of a quality that would actually detect an error.
what_to_review: Completeness of the reconciliation inventory against the trial balance
Preparer and reviewer independence and sign-off timing
Ageing and nature of reconciling items
Treatment of unexplained differences and plug entries
High-risk accounts — suspense, clearing, intercompany, cash
procedures: Reconcile the list of accounts reconciled to the full trial balance and identify accounts never reconciled.
Sample reconciliations and reassess whether reconciling items are genuinely explained or merely labelled.
Age reconciling items and test the oldest; items older than a quarter usually indicate an unresolved error.
Test sign-off timing — reviews dated the same minute as preparation are not reviews.
Test suspense and clearing accounts for balances that should have cleared.
red_flags: Reconciling items described as "timing" for months
Reviewer and preparer the same person
Accounts with a balance but no owner
Plug entries used to force agreement
plain: A reconciliation is how you prove a balance is real. Done badly, errors and theft sit undisturbed for years.

risk: The close is compressed to hit a reporting deadline, so controls are skipped and errors are found after the numbers are published.
audit_objective: Assess whether the close timetable allows controls to operate and whether it is actually followed.
what_to_review: Close calendar, task ownership and dependencies
Whether control activities have time allocated or are assumed
Late adjustments after the reported close
Sub-ledger cut-off and closing sequence
Post-close error identification and restatement history
procedures: Compare the close calendar to actual completion timestamps and identify tasks completed after the close was declared.
Extract entries posted after the reported close date and test their nature and approval.
Review the history of post-close adjustments and any restatements for a pattern.
Test whether sub-ledgers were closed before the general ledger in each period.
red_flags: Journals posted days after results were reported
Controls scheduled to run after the numbers are released
Recurring late adjustments from the same location
Deadline met by deferring reconciliations
evidence: Close calendar and task completion data
plain: When the close is rushed to hit a deadline, the checks are the first thing dropped.

risk: Estimates are set to deliver a desired result rather than a faithful one, and the assumptions behind them are never challenged.
audit_objective: Assess whether significant estimates are supportable, consistently applied and independently challenged.
what_to_review: Inventory of significant estimates and who owns each
Assumption setting, documentation and approval
Consistency of methodology between periods
Back-testing of prior estimates against outcomes
Governance — who challenges the estimate before it is booked
procedures: Back-test material estimates against subsequent actual outcomes and quantify the directional bias.
Test whether methodology or assumption changes coincided with pressure on results.
Trace significant estimates to documented approval by someone other than the preparer.
Compare the range of reasonable outcomes to the point estimate booked and assess where in the range management sits.
red_flags: Estimates consistently proving favourable on back-testing
Assumptions changed in the period they most helped
Point estimates always at the favourable end of the range
No documented challenge in committee minutes
evidence: Prior period estimates and actual outcomes
plain: Estimates are the numbers management gets to choose. That is exactly why they need challenging.

risk: Intercompany balances do not eliminate and consolidation adjustments are made outside the system, so group results contain errors nobody can trace.
audit_objective: Confirm that consolidation is complete, accurate and traceable from subsidiary ledgers to group accounts.
what_to_review: Completeness of entities consolidated and the group structure used
Intercompany matching, disputes and elimination differences
Top-side and consolidation journals outside the subsidiary ledgers
Minority interests, equity accounting and group structure changes
Audit trail from group numbers back to source ledgers
procedures: Reconcile the entities consolidated to the legal entity register and identify omissions or dormant inclusions.
Age unmatched intercompany balances and test how differences were resolved — write-off to income is a red flag.
Extract consolidation-level journals and test support and approval for each material entry.
Trace a sample of group balances back through consolidation to subsidiary ledgers.
red_flags: Intercompany differences written off to income
Top-side entries posted only at group with no subsidiary record
Entities appearing or disappearing without documented rationale
Consolidation performed in a spreadsheet outside the system
evidence: Group structure and legal entity register
plain: Group accounts are built by combining many companies. If balances between them do not cancel out, the group figures are wrong.

risk: Exchange rates are applied inconsistently or manually overridden, misstating results and equity in ways that are hard to detect.
audit_objective: Confirm exchange rates used are authorised, correctly sourced and consistently applied.
what_to_review: Rate source, upload process and authorisation
Application of spot, average and closing rates by balance type
Manual rate overrides at transaction level
Translation of net investments and the currency translation reserve
Hedge accounting interaction where applicable
procedures: Agree rates loaded into the system to the independent source for a sample of periods.
Test manual rate overrides by user and value.
Recompute translation for a sample of foreign subsidiaries including the movement in the translation reserve.
Test that the correct rate type is applied to each balance category.
red_flags: Rates uploaded by the person who benefits from the result
Overrides applied to individual large transactions
Translation reserve movements not explained
Average rates used where closing rates are required
plain: Using the wrong exchange rate quietly changes profit, and it is very hard to spot from the outside.

risk: The financial statements omit or misstate disclosures, or the narrative reporting is inconsistent with the numbers behind it.
audit_objective: Confirm the financial statements are complete, internally consistent and supported.
what_to_review: Disclosure checklist completion and who reviews it
Support for each disclosure traced to underlying records
Consistency between narrative reporting and the financial statements
Going concern assessment and its support
Review and approval by audit committee and board
procedures: Test a sample of disclosures back to underlying support rather than to the prior year statements.
Test the consistency of figures quoted in the narrative report against the financial statements.
Review the going concern assessment, including the forecast and sensitivities used.
Test that the disclosure checklist was completed for the current framework, not a superseded one.
red_flags: Disclosures rolled forward from last year with figures updated only
Narrative metrics that cannot be reconciled to the accounts
Going concern paper prepared after the accounts were drafted
Checklist signed but sections left blank
plain: The notes in the accounts are part of the accounts. Getting them wrong is a reporting failure, not a formatting one.

subprocess: Chart of Accounts and Ledger Master Data
risk: The chart of accounts is amended without control, so transactions are misclassified and reporting hierarchies silently change.
audit_objective: Confirm ledger master data changes are authorised and do not distort reporting.
what_to_review: Authorisation of account creation, blocking and hierarchy changes
Mapping of accounts to reporting lines and its integrity
Dormant and duplicate accounts
Posting restrictions on control and system accounts
Cost centre and profit centre master data
procedures: Extract chart of accounts changes for the period and test authorisation, particularly hierarchy remapping.
Test whether reporting hierarchy changes were reflected in comparatives and explained.
Identify accounts allowing direct posting that should be system-controlled, such as control accounts.
Review dormant accounts with sudden activity.
red_flags: Hierarchy changes made mid-year without restating comparatives
Direct posting permitted to reconciliation control accounts
Duplicate accounts for the same purpose
Accounts created by the person who then posts to them
plain: If accounts in the ledger can be changed freely, the reports built on them stop meaning what people think.

risk: Transactions with related parties are not identified, so they escape disclosure and are conducted on terms that would not survive scrutiny.
audit_objective: Confirm related parties are identified completely and their transactions are approved, priced and disclosed.
what_to_review: Completeness of the related party register and how it is maintained
Declarations from directors and key management
Identification of transactions with related parties in the ledger
Approval and pricing of related party transactions
Disclosure in the financial statements
procedures: Build an independent list of related parties from directorships, shareholdings and declarations, and compare to the register.
Match the related party list against customer and vendor masters and extract transactions.
Test identified transactions for approval by those without an interest, and for arm's length pricing.
Reconcile disclosed related party transactions to the ledger extract.
red_flags: Register maintained only from voluntary declarations
Related party found in the vendor master but not the register
Transactions approved by the interested party
Disclosure limited to remuneration
plain: Deals with people connected to the business must be disclosed. Hiding them is where governance scandals usually start.

risk: The board and management make decisions on reports whose figures cannot be reconciled to the ledger or whose definitions shift over time.
audit_objective: Confirm that management and board reporting is accurate, consistent and reconcilable.
what_to_review: Reconciliation of management reporting to statutory ledgers
Definition and stability of key performance measures
Non-financial and alternative performance measures and their basis
Manual manipulation of reports outside the system
Timeliness and completeness of reporting to the board
procedures: Reconcile key figures in the board pack to the general ledger and quantify differences.
Test whether definitions of key measures changed and whether comparatives were restated.
Trace alternative performance measures to their calculation and assess whether adjustments are consistently applied.
Identify where board reporting is assembled manually in spreadsheets and test controls over those models.
red_flags: Board figures that cannot be reconciled to the ledger
Adjusted measures excluding costs that recur every year
Definitions changed without restating prior periods
Board pack built by one person with no review
plain: The board makes decisions from these reports. If the numbers cannot be traced back to the ledger, the decisions rest on nothing.
